also.title: Donald Trump has sold out Ukraine. He makes appeaser Chamberlain look like a man of iron principle | Simon Tisdall

explained.headline: Ukraine reports Starlink restrictions despite Donald Trump's claims

happened.text: Ukraine is still recording connection issues with the Starlink satellite network after United States President Donald Trump said Elon Musk had reversed limits on the uplink.
Donald Trump stated that the tech billionaire had put the service back, though he declined to confirm whether he had directly asked for the restrictions to be lifted.
Defence ministry sources in Ukraine said that there was currently no confirmation that the speed restrictions had actually been lifted.

background.text: Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield are communication networks utilizing thousands of satellites to provide connectivity on the battlefield and in remote areas.
Earlier, reports emerged that Elon Musk had capped connection speeds for Ukrainian hardware, rendering some offensive and interceptor drones virtually useless.

These technical disputes occurred amid a diplomatic row between Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky regarding Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and US deals on Russian diesel.

matters.text: Sources within the Ukrainian defence ministry stated that the connection losses at high speeds were actively hampering military operations.
United States Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal announced that he had opened an inquiry into the matter.

uncertain.text: It remains disputed who originally ordered the restrictions, with Elon Musk previously suggesting the US military and president were behind any limits, while the White House and the Pentagon denied directing any changes.
A senior European official stated that Ukraine has not received a clear official explanation regarding who ordered the restrictions or why.

terms.definition: A satellite internet constellation operated by American aerospace company SpaceX.
An American aerospace manufacturer and space transportation services company.

problems: The text mentions US deals on Russian diesel without prior context or explanation.
The text assumes the reader knows about a diplomatic row that is not explained.

happened.text: Israeli forces killed two alleged Palestinian attackers at a checkpoint after multiple people were wounded.

background.text: The military operation comes shortly before parliamentary elections are scheduled to take place in Israel.

matters.text: Benjamin Netanyahu stated that security forces had successfully prevented a major terrorist attack that threatened civilians.
Right-wing politicians reportedly attempt to gain voter support by promising a harsh approach against Palestinian violence.

uncertain.text: No detailed information was initially provided regarding the specific target of the suspected attack.
Opinion polls suggest that it could be difficult for either Benjamin Netanyahu's camp or the opposition to secure a majority.

sources.title: Macron to meet student groups: Where are France’s protests heading?
France's Macron says 'illegitimate' protests will be banned in coming days

explained.headline: French student protests prompt security bans and government talks

happened.text: French President Emmanuel Macron plans to meet with high school student representatives as the country braces for further protests over the weekend.
Jean-Didier Berger, the minister delegate to the interior minister, said the police presence on the streets would be increased by 20 percent.

background.text: Emmanuel Macron is the French president whose government faces political deadlock and mounting debt.

matters.text: Observers suggest that a few minor measures cannot address the deeper anxieties regarding job prospects and the decline of state services.

Jacques Reland, a senior research fellow at the Global Policy Institute, stated that the root cause is that young people's prospects depend on family wealth because the wealthy family has replaced the welfare state.
Reland also stated that protesters are demanding financial support that the government cannot provide without increasing the deficit or touching social security, which would provoke further protests.

uncertain.text: It remains to be seen how the government can successfully bring young people off the streets.
Student groups and unions continue to mobilize and hold rallies despite government demonstration bans.
Whether upcoming talks between authorities, unions and student representatives will yield concrete solutions is yet to be decided.

removed.text: High school students have been protesting since September against teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and dilapidated school buildings.
Authorities announced curfews and protest bans in several cities following weekend demonstrations that escalated into violence, looting and clashes with police.
why: Evidence says authorities recommend not demonstrating; does not explicitly confirm city-wide bans or curfews.

removed.text: The student grievances have since expanded into a nationwide movement addressing the cost of living and deteriorating public services ahead of the presidential election.
why: Evidence does not mention the upcoming presidential election.

Taiwan braces as El Nino-supercharged Typhoon Champi approaches island

explained.headline: Typhoon Champi disrupts Taiwan and Japan as severe storm approaches

happened.text: Powerful Typhoon Champi swept close to Taiwan's north-east coast on Friday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations across the region.
Authorities reported that one person died after being swept away by waves, while 171 people were injured and 1,000 were forced to evacuate.

background.text: Taiwan's Central Weather Administration is the government agency monitoring the storm's trajectory alongside weather agencies in Hong Kong and Japan.

matters.text: Weather agencies forecast that Champi will bring strong winds and 90cm of rain to Taiwan's north-east until Saturday.
After passing Taiwan and the Okinawa islands, the storm is expected to hover over waters off China's eastern coast before moving towards Japan's main island.
Central Weather Administration Administrator Lu Kuo-chen stated that if the storm slows down as it approaches Taiwan's northeastern tip, its impact will last longer.

uncertain.text: Weather agencies in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Japan expect the eye of the storm to pass without making landfall in Taiwan.
However, a forecaster in Taiwan's Central Weather Administration told Reuters that a direct hit could not be ruled out entirely if the storm stalls, loops or wobbles.

terms.definition: A naturally occurring climate pattern involving the warming of surface waters in the tropical Pacific Ocean, which can trigger extreme weather events.
A mature tropical cyclone that develops in the western part of the North Pacific Ocean.
A governmental agency responsible for meteorological observation, forecasting, and warning services.

removed.text: Schools, offices, and Taiwan's stock exchange suspended operations on Friday, and power cuts affected nearly 8,400 households in Japan's Okinawa prefecture.
Typhoon Champi reached peak strength earlier in the week as the planet's strongest storm of the year, attaining maximum sustained winds equivalent to a Category 5 hurricane.
The storm has been fuelled by a Super El Niño, a naturally occurring phenomenon that heats the Pacific Ocean and contributes to active typhoon seasons.
